edges.subject: GRN
edges.quote: Heterozygous mutations in GRN gene lead to insufficient levels of the progranulin (PGRN) protein, resulting in frontotemporal dementia (FTD) with TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) inclusions, classified pathologically as frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD-TDP).

edges.subject: GRN
edges.quote: Homozygous GRN mutations are exceedingly rare and cause neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis 11, a lysosomal storage disease with onset in young adulthood, or an FTD syndrome with late-onset manifestations.

edges.subject: frontotemporal dementia
edges.quote: In this review, we highlight the broad spectrum of clinical phenotypes associated with PGRN deficiency, including primary progressive aphasia and behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia.
